study type: Qualitative study with descriptive exploratory design
exposure: Planning a vaginal breech birth (VBB) for a baby remaining breech after external cephalic version
outcome: Women's experiences of decision-making processes regarding mode of birth
Themes related to seeking VBB (reacting to a loss of choice and control, wanting trustworthy information, fighting the system and seeking support, importance of 'having a go')
cohort: Twenty-two women (n=22), three-quarters primiparous, who planned a vaginal breech birth and had given birth at one of two Australian maternity hospitals that supported VBB.
finding: Women seeking a vaginal breech birth value clear, consistent, and relevant information in deciding about mode of birth and desire autonomy and support for their choice with high quality care.
mod_finding: Of the women who planned a vaginal breech birth, 55% (n=12) had a vaginal birth and 45% (n=10) had a caesarean section after labor commenced.
